summary: Intro discovery for Redwood PLG quickstart. Citrine is evaluating Redwood Hosted for quick time-to-first-token and potential later move to Dedicated/Private for data-sensitive workloads. Main asks: free credits, sample cURL to measure time-to-first-token, perf baseline (latency/cost), and security docs (SOC2, KMS). Agreed next steps: send pricing/quickstart, share benchmark template, customer to run sandbox tests.
transcript: 00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. We wanted to run through the PLG quickstart, free credits, and make sure you can get to first token quickly. 00:18 Samir Rao: Great, thanks Alex. I'm Samir, CTO at Citrine. We've got Emily and Jordan here; our SRE Avery might jump in too. We're evaluating hosted first; curious about the free credits and how fast your API can get us a first token, like out-of-box latency. 00:35 Priya Patel: Yeah totally, quick note - the quickstart is designed to be self-serve. We give a small pool of free credits, a sandbox project in the console, and a cURL snippet that shows time-to-first-token including warmup. 00:50 Emily Wong: When you say warmup, do you mean model cold-start? We have some concerns about tail latency on first requests. 00:57 Priya Patel: Correct, cold-start can be noticeable on underutilized infra; for hosted we mitigate with fast cold-starts and a small keep-alive. For production you'd look at dedicated or pre-warmed pools. For the quickstart sandbox you should see first-token in the 500ms-1.5s range depending on model and sequence length. 01:18 Jordan Lee: That's helpful. What's the difference for us between hosted and dedicated—besides cost? If we start hosted and then move to dedicated later is that difficult? 01:27 Alex Chen: Good question. Hosted is easiest for PLG—zero infra, quick onboarding. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity, SLOs, and data isolation. Migration is supported: model pinning and identical API surface, so code changes are minimal. 01:39 Samir Rao: And private? We have some regulated clients who want VPC or on-prem. 01:44 Alex Chen: Redwood Private is an option—VPC peering and on-prem packaged control plane. That's typically an enterprise conversation and we would pair SE and infra early. 01:56 Emily Wong: Security: do you have SOC 2 and KMS support? We need audit logs and SSO. 02:02 Priya Patel: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II, SSO/SAML integrations, and KMS/HSM key integrations. For the quickstart we'll share a redacted security pack; for dedicated/private we provide full compliance docs. 02:14 Avery Park: Question about data retention: if we call hosted API for evaluation, is any PII ever stored? 02:19 Alex Chen: By default hosted logs are retained for billing and debugging, but you can opt-out and use ephemeral logs. We also offer customer-managed keys and retention policies for Dedicated/Private. We'll include exact retention SLAs in the docs we send. 02:34 Emily Wong: Great. On the perf side, can you share a benchmark template? We want to measure cost per 1k tokens and per-request latency with our prompts. 02:41 Priya Patel: Absolutely. I'll share a spreadsheet and a small benchmark harness. For quickstart we'll give sample prompts, token accounting notes, and a curl/snippet that measures time-to-first-byte, time-to-first-token, and full response time. 02:58 Jordan Lee: Are there demo limits or rate limits in sandbox? 03:01 Alex Chen: Sandbox has caps to prevent abuse but they're generous enough for realistic perf tests. We'll lay out quotas in the quickstart email. 03:09 Samir Rao: Competitors—are you seeing customers choose Redwood over OpenAI or Anthropic for this use-case? 03:14 Alex Chen: Yes, we often win on predictable latency and cost controls—teams that want control over unit economics and later options to move to dedicated/private. We sometimes lose to public APIs when customers prioritize raw model family or a single-provider lock-in. 03:30 Emily Wong: For the quickstart, what's the typical time-to-first-token for a small chat prompt? 03:34 Priya Patel: In our hosted setup you can expect ~600-1200ms for average small prompts; first token varies more on cold caches. Once warmed, 150-400ms is typical depending on model size and region. 03:47 Jordan Lee: And quantization/throughput—any tooling to suggest quantized model recommendations? 03:51 Alex Chen: Our Optimize toolkit suggests quantization and batching settings based on workload; SEs can run a quick analysis once you share a sample workload. 03:59 Samir Rao: Pricing—how is hosted priced? Per-token like others? Any reserved discounts? 04:05 Alex Chen: Hosted is usage-based per-token for generation and per-embedding unit for embeddings. Dedicated is committed capacity with monthly/annual contracts and discounts; Private is enterprise licensing. We'll send a pricing sheet with examples aligned to your benchmark. 04:20 Emily Wong: For our evaluation we want to: 1) get free credits to run baseline, 2) run time-to-first-token and avg latency tests, 3) evaluate cost per 1k tokens, 4) review security docs. 04:33 Alex Chen: Sounds good—I'll email the quickstart guide and pricing. Priya will push the benchmark and cURL. 04:39 Priya Patel: I'll include a sample python script as well that uses the SDK and prints timing metrics with token breakdown. 04:46 Jordan Lee: One more nit—if we hit a rate limit during testing, do you provide guidance on how to interpret results? 04:52 Priya Patel: Yes, we'll include notes on warmup, batching artifacts, and how to repeat runs for stable numbers. Also best practices for measuring cold-starts vs steady state. 05:01 Samir Rao: Ok, timeline—if we get the quickstart today, how long to have meaningful numbers? 05:06 Alex Chen: Typically teams get initial numbers same day or within 24 hours; for more thorough tests you want a week to get steady-state measurements. 05:14 Emily Wong: Great. Could you include a sample contract template for Dedicated? We might want that ahead of time. 05:20 Alex Chen: We'll surface the standard reserved capacity terms; legal is fine to share redlines after initial interest. 05:26 Jordan Lee: Any gotchas we should watch for when running the cURL? 05:29 Priya Patel: Watch prompt length and tokenization; include the exact same prompt each run, ensure you clear any local caches and measure cold vs warm by running isolated requests. 05:41 Samir Rao: Cool. Anything on on-prem hardware requirements for Private? 05:45 Alex Chen: For on-prem we'd discuss GPU SKUs, network egress, and private control plane sizing; that's typically part of a technical deep dive. 05:53 Alex Chen: Quick recap: Alex sends pricing & quickstart with free credits; Priya shares benchmark harness, sample cURL/python, and security redacted pack; Citrine spins up sandbox and runs tests, reports back next week; schedule deeper technical deep dive if they plan Dedicated/Private. 06:10 Emily Wong: Sounds good, thanks. 06:12 Samir Rao: Thanks Alex, Priya. We'll try to get initial numbers by next week. 06:17 Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with artifacts and a calendar invite for the deep dive if needed. 06:22 [call ends]
